items.passage: Meg's family has a big dog, Max, and a small gray cat. One evening, Meg was doing her homework in the kitchen. Mom was cooking fish for dinner. Then Mom went to the living room for a minute. The cat was watching the fish carefully. It walked quietly across the floor. When Meg looked up, the cat was on the table! It grabbed a piece of fish and jumped down. Max saw the cat and barked loudly. He chased the cat around the kitchen. The cat ran under the table, but Max was too big. Max could not reach it. Under the table, the cat ate the fish happily. Mom hurried back and laughed. 'That cat is a clever thief,' she said. 'We must not leave fish on the table.' Then she gave Max a piece of chicken for his help. Now Meg always watches the cat carefully when Mom is cooking.

items.passage: Folding paper is a fun hobby for kids and adults. With just one piece of paper, you can make animals, flowers, and boats. You do not need scissors, glue, or a lot of money. Many kids enjoy folding paper after school. It is easy to start. First, choose a square piece of paper. Then follow the pictures in a book, step by step. Each picture shows one step. If you fold slowly and carefully, your animal will look great. If you hurry, the paper may not fold in the right place. My friend Ben has made many paper animals. His first frog did not look like a frog at all. He finished it in just one minute. After he made ten more frogs, he got much better. Now his paper frogs can even jump when you push their backs. Folding paper has some good points. It is quiet, so you can do it on a rainy day. It also helps you think and use your hands well. You can give your paper animals to friends as gifts. Have you ever tried it? Find a piece of paper and start today!

items.passage: The person who I admire most is my grandmother. She has run a small bookstore in our town for forty years. The store, which is next to the bus station, is full of old and new books. It was opened by her father a long time ago. It looks like an ordinary store, but it is always busy. Kids who live near the store visit it after school. My grandmother lets them read any book for free. When a child asks for help with a hard word, she never refuses. She always helps. She can recognize every kid who comes into the store. I do not know how she remembers all their names. She often gives them books which they will enjoy. However, her eyes have become weak these days. Now she wears thick glasses, and small words look like ants to her. So the kids who visit the store read books aloud to her. She listens with a big smile and helps them with hard words. Last month, a young boy read his first English book to her. She was very proud of him. The store has become a happy place for everyone in town. I hope that I can be kind like her one day.

The writer's grandmother has weak eyes, so she does not work at her store now.

items.passage: Every Saturday morning, a yellow bus filled with books travels to small towns in the countryside. Many of these towns do not have a library, and bookstores are far away. The bus was started three years ago by local teachers who wanted every kid to enjoy books. Although the bus is not very large, it carries more than five hundred books. When the bus arrives, smiling kids run out of their houses. Their parents often come too. Some of them wait in a long line before the doors open. Inside the bus, kids can sit on a soft carpet and read quietly. A volunteer who drives the bus also reads stories aloud to the younger kids. Each kid can borrow three books at a time and return them the next week. Tess, a girl who lives in one of the towns, has borrowed over fifty books this year. 'The bus is the place where I found my favorite book,' she said. Now she wants to become a writer. Families in the community really appreciate the bus. However, the program needs more help. The bus is getting old, and the teachers need money to repair it. They have started a campaign to raise money, and anyone can contribute. They are also looking for volunteers who can read to kids on weekends. With a little help, the yellow bus can keep bringing smiles to many more kids.
items.prompt: Why did the writer write this article?
options: to explain how to drive a large bus
to sell old books to families in the countryside
to talk about a book bus and ask for help
to talk about a new library in a big city

items.passage: Should students be allowed to bring phones to school? At my school, phones are not allowed at all, and many students do not like this rule. Some adults argue that phones only bring trouble to classrooms. In my opinion, students should be allowed to bring phones, but they should not use them during class. First of all, phones can help students stay safe. Many students walk home alone or take the bus after school. If there is a problem on the way home, they can call their parents right away. Moreover, a phone with a map can help young students find their way. Parents also feel calm when they know their kids can call them. Also, phones can help students learn. Students can search for new words or check a fact in a short time. Our teachers used to bring heavy dictionaries to class, but now a phone can do the same job. Of course, phones can also cause problems. Some students play games or send texts during class. This is why phones should be kept in a box during lessons. Teachers can give them back at lunch or after school. Students must learn to be responsible for their own phones. In this way, students can keep their phones in order to stay safe, and classes can stay quiet. In conclusion, I believe that phones should be allowed at school with clear rules. Phones are not good or bad by themselves. It depends on how we use them. A good rule can protect both students and lessons. I hope our school will consider this idea.
items.prompt: What does the writer do in this text?
options: The writer tells events in time order.
The writer gives reasons for an opinion.
The writer explains how a phone works.
